meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Viet Nam (unitary State; enterprise registration and investment licensing administered at the central level and delegated to provincial Departments of Planning and Investment)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (socialist legal tradition with French-derived commercial and administrative codification)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Viet Nam–Republic of Korea Bilateral Investment Treaty
Viet Nam–Germany Bilateral Investment Treaty (and comparable legacy BITs with other EU Member States)

Double Taxation Agreements with more than 80 jurisdictions, including Singapore, Japan, the Republic of Korea, the People's Republic of China, Australia and the United Kingdom; no comprehensive DTA between Viet Nam and the United States

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 (as amended by Law No. 03/2022/QH15 and Law No. 12/2022/QH15); Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14; Law on Prevention and Combating Money Laundering No. 14/2022/QH15 (effective 1 March 2023); Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP on enterprise registration; Decree No. 31/2021/ND-CP detailing the Law on Investment; Decree No. 102/2022/ND-CP defining beneficial ownership for AML/CFT purposes; Circular No. 09/2023/TT-NHNN of the State Bank of Viet Nam guiding AML/CFT measures; Circular No. 215/2016/TT-BTC on enterprise registration fees.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (beneficial ownership data is collected by enterprises and reporting entities, retained in the National Business Registration Database, and provided to the State Bank of Viet Nam, the Anti-Money Laundering Information Center, and competent investigative authorities; no public UBO register is accessible to the general public)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport or national identity document of each individual shareholder and of the proposed legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent authority in the investor's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Viet Nam has been a Contracting Party to the HCCH Apostille Convention since 22 January 2011), followed by certified Vietnamese notarized translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing / legal existence, and current corporate register extract of the corporate investor, if the shareholder is a legal entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or equivalent competent corporate authority in the investor's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for documents originating from non-Apostille Contracting States, Vietnamese consular legalization at the Vietnamese Embassy/Consulate, followed by certified Vietnamese notarized translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the Vietnamese law firm and/or authorized signatories to prepare and submit the pre-incorporation dossier and to obtain the Investment Registration Certificate and Enterprise Registration Certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign investor and notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Vietnamese consular legalization, followed by certified Vietnamese notarized translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution or written consent of the corporate investor approving the establishment of the Viet Nam limited liability company, the charter capital amount, the capital contribution schedule, and the appointment of the legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors / shareholders' general meeting of the corporate investor in its home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Vietnamese consular legalization, followed by certified Vietnamese notarized translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter, source-of-funds statement, or audited financial statements of the investor, only when requested by the provincial Department of Planning and Investment to substantiate investment capital and economic substance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank or registered auditor in the investor's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille and certified Vietnamese notarized translation where invoked by the investment registration authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, directors, legal representatives, and authorized signatories against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, Viet Nam's domestic AML/CFT notifications, the State Bank of Viet Nam's counter-terrorism and proliferation-financing lists, the World Bank and Asian Development Bank debarment registers, and, where applied by international correspondent banks, the OFAC SDN list and EU Consolidated Sanctions List. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) comprise domestic, foreign, and international-organization PEPs, including their family members and close associates, as defined under Articles 3 and 4 of Decree No. 102/2022/ND-CP and Circular No. 09/2023/TT-NHNN. Enhanced due diligence and source-of-wealth verification is triggered where any 25%-or-greater beneficial owner is a PEP; the business relationship must be monitored continuously and records retained for at least five years after the relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Business Registration Portal (Cổng thông tin quốc gia về đăng ký doanh nghiệp) – https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn; name clearance is executed as an integrated component of the Enterprise Registration Certificate application lodged electronically on that Portal or physically with the provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) having territorial jurisdiction over the proposed head office.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered enterprise name must be written entirely in Vietnamese, including the compulsory legal-form indicator 'CÔNG TY TNHH' (or the full form 'Công ty trách nhiệm hữu hạn'). The proper name component must be composed of letters of the Vietnamese alphabet, must be pronounceable, and may include only numerals and symbols such as '&', '.', ',', '+', '-'. Foreign words, including English brand terms such as 'ASO', 'SEO', 'GROWTH' or 'LOCALIZATION', may be used only if transliterated into Vietnamese script or if accompanied by a distinctive Vietnamese proper name; the authority registers the Vietnamese name as authoritative, and any non-Vietnamese display name is treated purely as a secondary presentation. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to a legally protected registered trademark or to an existing enterprise in the national database.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words identical or confusingly similar to a name of an already-registered enterprise or of an enterprise whose dissolution is pending.

Terms suggesting affiliation with or approval by state administrative agencies, the National Assembly, People's Committees, the armed forces, political organizations, social-political organizations, or international organizations without lawful authorization (e.g., 'BỘ', 'TỔNG CỤC', 'SỞ', 'UBND', 'TÊN LỰC LƯỢNG VŨ TRANG').
Names contrary to the historical traditions, culture, national identity, ethics, or customs of Viet Nam.
Words or symbols that lack meaning, are unpronounceable, or comprise no intelligible Vietnamese-language element.
General designations standing alone as the proper name (e.g., 'LOCALIZATION', 'SEARCH', 'GROWTH') without a distinctive additional proper-name component.

Terms indicating conditional business lines requiring prior ministerial licensing or satisfaction of market-access conditions, such as 'NGÂN HÀNG' (bank), 'BẢO HIỂM' (insurance), 'CHỨNG KHOÁN' (securities), 'QUỸ ĐẦU TƯ' (investment fund), 'KIỂM TOÁN' (audit), unless the required license or pre-approval is already obtained.
Terms containing the words 'CỘNG HÒA', 'XÃ HỘI', 'NHÂN DÂN' in a manner implying state sovereignty or agency status.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Viet Nam does not operate a standalone pre-registration name-reservation mechanism; name clearance is consolidated into the Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC) application procedure. Under Article 26 of Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP, the DPI must issue the ERC or a written notice of rejection within 03 working days of receiving a complete dossier. If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may: (1) resubmit a revised ERC application on the National Business Registration Portal proposing an alternative available name, curing the identified defects within the statutory resubmission window; (2) file a first-instance administrative complaint to the Director of the provincial DPI within 90 days of receiving the rejection notice, pursuant to the Law on Complaints No. 02/2011/QH13, with the DPI obliged to respond within 15 days; (3) elevate a second complaint to the provincial People's Committee or commence an administrative action in the competent provincial People's Court if the first-instance resolution is unsatisfactory; and (4) simultaneously request an informal re-screening advisory through the name-availability search facility on the National Business Registration Portal. There is no statutorily renewable name reservation, so the applicant should lodge the ERC promptly after the initial name-availability confirmation is received.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as a statutory head-office. Article 41 of the Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 requires the head office to be a legitimate physical address located in Vietnamese territory where the enterprise conducts its main business and which is used as the official postal address for legal service; a post-office box or a purely virtual mailbox without a physical landing is not acceptable. For a low-risk ISIC 7310 app-growth agency, 'serviced-office' or 'registered-address' arrangements operated by a licensed provider are tolerated in practice in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City provided the provider genuinely receives legal process, maintains records, and permits authority access; however, the DPI increasingly requests a copy of the lease agreement or land-title certificate, and the address must be identifiable by the national addressing system.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-Moderate – approximately 15% annual probability for a non-conditional, low-reputation-risk digital-services LLC. The provincial DPI and inter-agency audit teams conduct post-registration verification, and a one-off address review frequently occurs within the first 12 months for foreign-invested enterprises with small charter capital and predominantly non-resident-sourced digital revenue. Additional physical verification may be triggered by banking KYC visits and by the issuance of an investment-registration certificate that flags the head-office address for confirmation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) legal preparation, dossier compilation, and submission to the provincial DPI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing private professional fee benchmark for a standard 100%-foreign-owned digital-services LLC; no separate State fee is charged for IRC issuance under the Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC) application, name-availability clearance, and statutory registration fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Law firm service fee plus the provincial DPI as collecting authority for the State fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed professional fee plus the statutory registration tariff of VND 100,000 (approximately USD 4) under Circular No. 215/2016/TT-BTC

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and/or Vietnamese consular legalization facilitation for the investor's identity documents, power of attorney, certificate of incorporation/good standing, and board resolution
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and apostille-issuing authority in the investor's home jurisdiction; Vietnamese Embassy/Consulate where consular legalization applies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory and consular fee schedules of the originating jurisdiction; average for four apodized documents excluding Vietnam-side translation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Vietnamese notarized translation of the incorporation bundle (passport/COI, POA, good-standing certificate, board resolution, and lease document)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Vietnamese notary public (Công chứng viên) and licensed translation service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Provincial notarial fee tariff of VND 10,000–50,000 per page plus market translation rates; estimated 20–30 total pages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO piercing, PEP, sanctions, and adverse-media due-diligence screening of all shareholders, directors, and authorized signatories
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Law firm compliance/KYC team and licensed data providers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market-benchmark flat professional fee for an ownership chain of up to four natural persons or corporate tiers

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered head-office due diligence: landlord title verification, lease review, and serviced-address arrangement confirmation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Law firm and the serviced-office provider/landlord
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a serviced-address package in Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City plus lease-confirmation legal review

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory name-search advisory, enterprise-name availability evaluation, and monitoring of the ERC name-clearance decision
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Law firm (State component included in the ERC line item)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency reserve for additional source-of-funds substantiation (bank reference letters, audited financial statements, or shareholder wealth evidence) requested by the DPI during pre-incorporation review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Estimated variable cost triggered only upon the authority's written request

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14, Articles 23, 26, 34 and 43; Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP on enterprise registration, Articles 12 to 19; Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14, Articles 30 and 38
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Business Registration Office under the Hanoi Department of Planning and Investment; online via the National Business Registration Portal at dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn; Investment Registration Division of the same Department for the Investment Registration Certificate
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form I-1 (Application for Enterprise Registration), Form I-2 (List of Members), and the Company Charter filed as a complete enterprise registration dossier
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a non-conditional service LLC in ISIC 7310; charter capital must be contributed in full within 90 days of the Enterprise Registration Certificate date under Article 75 of the Law on Enterprises; no escrow or capital verification certificate is required by law
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF MEMBERS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY ADOPTED BY THE FIRST MEETING OF MEMBERS HELD AT THE REGISTERED OFFICE ON [DATE]. 1. PRELIMINARY DECLARATIONS: the Meeting is attended by all members or authorized representatives holding one hundred percent of the charter capital; the Meeting is lawfully convened under Article 56 of the Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14; Mr. [NAME] chairs the Meeting and Ms. [NAME] acts as secretary. 2. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: the Board of Members confirms the total charter capital of VND [AMOUNT], divided into [NUMBER] contributed portions; each member subscribes to the schedule in the List of Members and irrevocably undertakes to pay the subscribed portion in full no later than ninety days after the ERC date. 3. ADOPTION OF THE CHARTER: the Company Charter annexed to this Resolution is unanimously approved and shall govern the constitution, governance and dissolution of the Company. 4. REGISTERED OFFICE: the registered office is fixed at [ADDRESS], Ha Noi City, Viet Nam; the Company does not prefix a branch at this stage. 5. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: the Board of Members appoints Mr. [NAME] as Chairman, Mr. [NAME] as General Director, and Mr. [NAME] as Chief Accountant, each with the powers and remuneration determined in the internal operating rules; legal representation is vested in the General Director. 6. CORPORATE GOVERNANCE: the corporate seal, bank accounts, statutory books and accounting system shall be set up in accordance with the Law on Enterprises, the Accounting Law No. 88/2015 and the Tax Administration Law No. 38/2019. 7. AUTHORIZATION: the General Director is authorized to file the enterprise registration dossier, to effect the publication of the registered contents, to sign the office lease and to obtain fire safety and environmental administrative clearances. 8. CLOSURE: this Resolution is executed in Vietnamese and English, takes effect immediately, and is certified by the Chairman and the secretary of the Meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name search and investment registration certificate (IRC) filing for foreign investors
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Business Registration Portal (dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn) for name reservation; Investment Registration Division of the Hanoi Department of Planning and Investment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The law firm verifies the proposed Vietnamese and English names through the National Business Registration Portal. A 100 percent foreign-owned LLC in advertising services must first obtain an IRC under the Law on Investment. The investment registration dossier is filed online or by post; the applicant must provide notarized copies of the investors' identity documents and the economic project plan. The DPI issues the IRC within 15 working days of receiving a complete dossier; the ERC references the IRC project code.
required_dossiers: Written investment registration application in the Form A-I-1
Legal status certificates of all foreign investors (notarized passport copies or certificate of incorporation)
Financial capacity statement of each investor
Investment project proposal with objectives, scale, location and implementation timetable
Certified copy of the office lease intention or counterparty agreement
Power of attorney if the application is filed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DPI issues a written request for revision, the applicant has 10 working days to supplement the dossier from the date of the request; failure to do so leads to return of the dossier. The applicant may resubmit after full correction, and an unlawful refusal can be challenged by an administrative complaint under the Law on Denunciation No. 25/2018 to the Chairman of the Hanoi People's Committee or by an administrative action at the Hanoi Administrative Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and submission of the enterprise registration dossier
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office under the Hanoi Department of Planning and Investment; online via the National Business Registration Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporation counsel drafts the Company Charter and the statutory forms. The dossier is signed by all members and their authorized signatories. The applicant uploads the complete set on the National Business Registration Portal and pays the online registration fee of VND 50,000 (approximately USD 2) via the integrated payment gateway; the portal returns an official acceptance stamp with file number. The paper filing fee is VND 100,000 (approximately USD 4) if filed in-person at the one-stop desk.
required_dossiers: Application for Enterprise Registration in the Form I-1
Company Charter executed by all members
List of Members in the Form I-2
Notarized or certified copies of the legal status documents of each member
Power of attorney appointing the authorized person to submit the dossier
Detailed list of capital contribution portion values if contributing different assets types
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The Business Registration Office may issue a written request for amendment within 3 working days; the applicant corrects and re-submits on the same portal. A refusal must be provided in writing with the legal ground and Article 5 of Decree 01/2021/ND-CP gives the applicant the right to amend and re-file or to file a complaint and administrative lawsuit against the refusal decision within the general administrative litigation time limits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of the Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC) and tax code activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office under the Hanoi Department of Planning and Investment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon completeness of the dossier, the Business Registration Office issues the Enterprise Registration Certificate within 3 working days. The ERC is a digital certificate bearing the enterprise code, enterprise tax code, employment insurance code, and all registered governance particulars; no separate tax registration application is needed. The legal representative receives the ERC through the portal and may download the soft copy for notarization.
required_dossiers: No additional filings; the ERC follows from the complete dossier in Step 2
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the authority refuses, the grounds must be written; the applicant may cure the defects and re-file immediately. Where the statutory deadline expires without a decision, the applicant may file a request to the Director of the Business Registration Office for a written outcome and thereafter initiate a complaint under the 2018 Law on Denunciation or an administrative lawsuit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate seal creation and seal notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed seal making entity; notification recorded on the National Business Registration Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Company creates its own seal without state approval under Article 43 of the Law on Enterprises. A licensed seal artisan produces the seal showing the company name and 13-digit tax code. The company signs the seal sample card, issues the internal policy on seal usage, and notifies the seal sample to the National Business Registration Portal after the ERC is issued; the seal enters into use after the notification receipt is generated.
required_dossiers: Enterprise Registration Certificate
Seal sample card signed by the legal representative
Executive decision approving the seal usage rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the portal rejects the seal notification due to facial inconsistency, the company corrects the sample and re-submits through the same function. The company may execute contracts without a seal in limited statutory cases, and the seal remains valid retroactively once the notification is recorded.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Business Registration Portal operated by the Business Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of the ERC, the company must publish on the National Business Registration Portal its registered name, ERC number, head office address, authorized capital, legal representative, and the content of its business lines. The administrative fee for publication is bundled in the registration fee; the portal generates a publication confirmation letter.
required_dossiers: ERC number
Company Charter summary
List of members information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late publication attracts an administrative penalty under Decree 50/2016/ND-CP as amended; the company can file a late publication and pay the penalty online. Should the portal fail to display the record due to internal error, the company requests an official confirmation letter from the Business Registration Office and retains evidence of the payment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, electronic invoice, social insurance and bank account post-registration proceedings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Hanoi Tax Department (electronic tax portal etax.gdt.gov.vn); Social Insurance Agency of Ha Noi; issuing commercial banks
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company registers an authorized digital signature (eToken) for tax filing, then completes the initial tax registration information and issues electronic invoices through a certified tax service provider; the employer registration with the social insurance agency is performed for every employee; the company opens an operating account in a Vietnamese bank and registers the account with the tax authority. For cross-border collections, the company may use corresponding banking rails such as Wise B2B or Payoneer as a secondary payment channel, and these balances must be reflected in the accounting books and tax filings.
required_dossiers: Enterprise Registration Certificate
Legal representative passport and digital signature certificate
Company seal sample
Office lease agreement
Employee list for social insurance registration
Designation of the domestic bank account and international payment rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the tax office sends a notice on discrepancies, the company corrects the declaration within the notice period; late registration is subject to interest and penalties under the Law on Tax Administration, but the taxpayer may apply for a reduction of penalties on grounds of force majeure. Social insurance registrations may be supplemented before contribution due dates; disputes are resolved through the social insurance complaint process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical premises clearances: fire safety, environmental protection registration and occupational safety
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Fire Prevention and Rescue Police Department of Ha Noi City Police (PC07); district-level Division of the Hanoi Department of Natural Resources and Environment; municipal Labor Inspectorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company finalizes the office lease and requests the building owner to provide either a valid fire safety approval certificate of the building or a tenant fit-out design approval dossier; the fire police carry out a site inspection and issue a handover acceptance letter. As the activity is an office-based service without manufacturing, the company completes the Environmental Protection Registration for a waste-generating service premise under Decree 08/2022/ND-CP, signs a solid waste collection contract with a licensed collector, and submits the occupational risk assessment and labor safety self-declaration to the labor inspectorate.
required_dossiers: Office lease agreement
Certified floor plan or fit-out drawing
Building fire safety certificate or separate fire safety approval dossier
Company ERC
Environmental protection registration declaration with waste data
Contract with licensed solid waste collector
Labor safety self-assessment report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire inspection identifies non-conformities, the company abates them within the prescribed period and presents corrective proof for re-inspection; if the DONRE refuses the environmental registration, the company amends the waste projection and re-files. Failure to comply triggers administrative fines, and the company may appeal the sanctioning decision under Chapter XII of Decree 08/2022/ND-CP.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for this non-industrial office activity; general industrial administration rests with the Hanoi Department of Industry and Trade, but no conditional industry license or industrial production permit is required for an ASO and SEO localization agency outside conditional sectors
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No separate operating license is mandated; the Enterprise Registration Certificate issued and the publication on the National Business Registration Portal constitute the lawful authorization to conduct ISIC 7310 services in Viet Nam

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Hanoi Department of Natural Resources and Environment (DONRE) - Environmental Protection Division; reference standard setter: Vietnam Environment Administration under MONRE
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA and Preliminary EIA; office-only service activity not listed under Decree 08/2022/ND-CP requiring an EIA or environmental permit, but subject to a simplified Environmental Protection Registration for premises generating municipal solid waste and domestic wastewater
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Domestic wastewater must comply with QCVN 14:2008/BTNMT if treated and discharged on site or be discharged into the municipal sewerage system in accordance with the building infrastructure permit; indoor and boundary air quality shall meet QCVN 06:2009/BTNMT; solid waste separation and collection must comply with Decree 08/2022/ND-CP and Circular 02/2022/TT-BTNMT; no VOC-specific threshold applies because the agency does not operate printing, chemical, adhesive, or industrial coating processes

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: the office fit-out must satisfy the fire prevention and fighting conditions of Decree 136/2020/ND-CP, evidenced by the building owner's fire safety certificate or a tenant-specific approval letter with on-site inspection; structural load compliance is certified by the lessor in the lease agreement; workplace clearance includes the employer labor safety declaration, occupational health risk assessment and employee safety training records under the Law on Occupational Safety and Health No. 84/2015/QH14

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Department of Taxation (Tổng cục Thuế) under the Ministry of Finance of the Socialist Republic of Viet Nam. Primary digital portals: eTax electronic tax declaration portal (https://thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn), National Electronic Invoice Portal (https://hoadondientu.gdt.gov.vn), National Business Registration Portal (https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn), and the Viet Nam Automated Cargo and Port Consolidated System (VNACCS/VCIS) for customs. Provincial Departments of Taxation (Cục Thuế) administer local LLC files; the Large Taxpayers Department manages enterprises classified as large.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Obtain an Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) from the provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) under the Law on Investment 2020 (Form A.1/A.2). For the ISIC 7310 advertising/agency sector, no conditional investment license is required. Step 2: Submit the enterprise registration dossier through the National Business Registration Portal; the DPI issues the Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC) within 3-15 working days. The 13-digit enterprise code printed on the ERC is automatically the statutory tax identification number (TIN/MST) and VAT identification number; no separate TIN application is required. Step 3: Within 10 working days of obtaining the ERC, file electronic tax registration records and the VAT method declaration on the eTax portal (Form 01-ĐK-TCT for the taxpayer, Form 02-ĐK-TCT for any branch or permanent establishment in Viet Nam, and Form 05/ĐK-HT for the VAT calculation method election). Step 4: Acquire a digital signature (USB token or remote e-signature) qualified by the Ministry of Information and Communications; register the e-invoice template and e-invoice issuance parameters with the General Department of Taxation. Step 5: Open a Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) at a Vietnamese licensed credit institution in the name of the LLC to record equity and loan inflows and to evidence repatriated export earnings. Failure to register within statutory deadlines results in penalties up to VND 25,000,000 for late tax registration plus a provisional tax assessment at the highest applicable rate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope. A foreign-invested LLC is a Vietnamese resident enterprise (incorporated in Viet Nam, central management in Viet Nam) and is subject to Corporate Income Tax (CIT) at entity level on its worldwide income at the statutory rate of 20%. The LLC is not a pass-through for Vietnamese tax purposes; there is no check-the-box regime and no taxation at the hand of the foreign members. Dividend distributions to foreign shareholders are generally exempt from further Vietnamese CIT withholding, but payments of interest, royalties, and service fees to offshore related parties remain subject to Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT) provisions. Non-resident enterprises deriving Vietnam-source income without a permanent establishment are taxed on a territorial basis by way of FCT withholding; a resident LLC is not eligible for that territorial regime for its own income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No entity classification election (no pass-through/check-the-box) exists in Vietnamese domestic law; tax personality is determined by the Enterprise Law. Available statutory elections: (i) VAT method election between credit method (compulsory for enterprises with annual revenue from sales and services of VND 1 billion or more, or opting voluntarily if adequate accounting) and direct method on value-added for smaller taxpayers; (ii) CIT incentives: the LLC may elect to claim preferential CIT rates (10% or 15% for up to 10-15 years) and tax holiday incentives if the project is located in an industrial park, economic zone, high-tech zone, or meets investment-scale criteria, subject to DPI/GDC registration; (iii) Double Tax Agreement (DTA) relief: the LLC can elect to claim foreign tax credit under the applicable DTA on its foreign-source income instead of a mere deduction; (iv) loss carry-forward: up to 5 consecutive years, applied in chronological order; (v) transfer pricing documentation: election between the simplified transfer pricing documentation regime for small/medium taxpayers with related-party transactions below VND 30 billion and the full three-tier documentation (master file, local file, country-by-country report) for multinational groups meeting the threshold; (vi) Global Minimum Tax and Qualified Domestic Minimum Top-up Tax (QDMTT) under Resolution 107/2023/QH15 for multinational enterprise groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million, effective fiscal year 2024. The ADC/SEO localization agency with typical revenue profile will not normally be captured by Pillar Two unless it belongs to a large international group.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax; Thuế Giá Trị Gia Tăng) as governed by the Law on Value Added Tax No. 13/2008/QH12, amended by Law No. 31/2013/QH13, Decree No. 209/2013/NĐ-CP and Circular No. 219/2013/TT-BTC. Export of goods and export of services consumed outside Viet Nam are zero-rated. Special consumption tax, natural resources tax, environmental protection tax and FCT are outside the scope of the VAT statement. Temporary VAT reduction from 10% to 8% for certain domestic goods and services was applied periodically under Government Decree No. 15/2022/NĐ-CP and subsequent extensions; the standard headline rate of 10% remains the applicable benchmark.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No VAT registration threshold applies to a foreign-invested LLC; every enterprise engaged in the supply of goods or services subject to VAT must register before commencing VAT-liable activities. For household businesses and individual business households, an annual taxable turnover not exceeding VND 100,000,000 is exempt from VAT (with the right to elect registration). The agency should register for VAT, choose the credit method if projected annual revenue is at least VND 1 billion, and register for e-invoicing immediately upon obtaining the ERC, notwithstanding any turnover threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: E-invoicing is mandatory since 1 July 2022 under Decree No. 123/2020/NĐ-CP and Circular No. 78/2021/TT-BTC. Every B2B and B2C export sale must be evidenced by an e-invoice in XML format carrying a digital signature and QR code. Two regimes coexist: (i) e-invoice with tax-authority code (hóa đơn điện tử có mã của cơ quan thuế): the taxpayer requests a clearance code in real time through the GDT e-invoice portal (SOAP/REST API), receives a code within milliseconds, and the invoice is valid only after the code is affixed; this regime is mandatory for first-time issuers (during the first 12 months of issuance) and for enterprises flagged as high-risk; (ii) self-generated e-invoice code (hóa đơn điện tử không có mã của cơ quan thuế): available only to VAT credit-method taxpayers with good compliance, issued in XML with own signature, transmitted to the National E-Invoice Portal at least monthly by the 20th of the following month (monthly submitters) or by the 25th of the following quarter (quarterly submitters). The GDT performs automated cross-matching of e-invoice data against VAT returns, customs export declarations, and bank payment credits, and API-based data exchange with the eTax system is mandatory. QR-code invoices must be readable by the official app to be accepted as export evidence.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Eligibility is governed by Article 9 of the Law on VAT and Article 16 of Circular 219/2013/TT-BTC. Goods: exported goods qualify for 0% VAT where the following cumulative conditions are met: (i) a written export contract with a foreign buyer; (ii) physical export of the goods from Viet Nam evidenced by an export customs declaration (VNACCS); (iii) payment for the exported goods is received from a foreign party through a licensed bank by non-cash transfer; (iv) the customs declaration and invoice match the payment. Services: offshore services, including advertising, App Store Optimization (ASO), search engine optimization, multilingual localization, and digital marketing, qualify for 0% VAT only where the service is provided to a foreign organization or individual and is consumed outside Viet Nam. Substantive conditions: (i) the recipient is a non-resident in Viet Nam and has no establishment in Viet Nam; (ii) the contract explicitly contemplates offshore consumption and delivery outside Viet Nam; (iii) payment is credited from abroad into the LLC's bank account in Viet Nam through a non-cash transfer (e.g., SWIFT MT103, Wise B2B credit, Payoneer rail that ultimately settles through a Viet Nam licensed bank); (iv) supporting evidence shows the actual use of the service overseas, such as Apple App Store Connect search ads reports, Google Ads geographic targeting and consumption reports, organic search rank monitors outside Viet Nam, localized app metadata delivered to foreign target markets, and third-party analytics. A 90-day rule applies to export goods: if the foreign payment is not received within 90 days from the date of the export customs declaration, the exporter must adjust the output VAT and reverse any VAT refund/zero-rating in the month in which payment is actually collected. The agency must also ensure that the VAT-free treatment is not lost by providing services that are re-supplied in Viet Nam or used for a Vietnamese taxable person.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Customs Declaration (electronically filed via VNACCS/VCIS for goods exports; not applicable to offshore services),
Commercial invoice / e-invoice XML with QR code and digital signature,
Export contract (signed by the LLC and the foreign principal), in English or Vietnamese with counterpart in the other language where necessary,
For goods: Bill of Lading / Air Waybill, packing list, insurance certificate, certificate of origin (if required),

For offshore services: service acceptance certificate or campaign completion report signed by the foreign client; App Store Connect / Google Play / Apple Search Ads / Google Ads consumption evidence; ASO keyword and localization delivery reports; server or platform logs showing overseas users,
Bank evidence of non-cash payment from abroad: credit advice from the Vietnamese bank, SWIFT MT103/MT202, or Wise B2B / Payoneer settlement confirmation referencing the invoice number,
Foreign currency inward remittance certificate issued by the Vietnamese bank / DICA credit record,
Tax declaration form (Tờ khai thuế GTGT) and VAT refund dossier (mẫu 01/GTGT, 01/GTTT) where the zero-rated input VAT refund is claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The General Department of Taxation prioritizes audit of zero-rated export transactions, particularly in digital services where no customs declaration exists. Under the Law on Tax Administration No. 38/2019/QH14 and Decree No. 125/2020/NĐ-CP, misreporting zero-rating or overstating VAT refunds triggers: (i) administrative fine of 20% of the under-declared/refunded tax amount where no fraudulent intent is proven, plus late-payment interest at 0.03% per day on the underpaid tax; (ii) fines from 1x to 3x the evaded tax amount for intentional false declaration or fraudulent refund; (iii) where the VAT refund is retroactively clawed back, the taxpayer must immediately repay the refunded cash plus interest, and the GDT may temporarily suspend the taxpayer's e-invoice issuance, place the enterprise on the blacklist, and impose the highest VAT rate on subsequent invoices; (iv) criminal liability under Article 200 of the Penal Code 2015 (amended 2017) for tax evasion from VND 100,000,000 upwards: imprisonment for up to 7 years for individuals, and for commercial legal entities fines up to VND 15 billion (and up to VND 20 billion for aggravating circumstances) plus suspension of operations for up to 3 years; (v) customs inspection may be retroactively extended to the 5-year tax audit window; in case of sham service transactions created through offshore payment rails, the transaction may be recharacterized as a deemed dividend or FCT-liable payment, with additional CIT, VAT, and FCT assessments. Exporters are also subject to State Bank foreign exchange examination: failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days (unless a longer contractual term is agreed and legally permissible) exposes the LLC to forced purchase/sale through the licensed bank and administrative penalties under the Ordinance on Foreign Exchange; repeated breaches can lead to suspension of the DICA and denial of inward remittance confirmation, which in turn would break the VAT zero-rating evidence chain.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) (Ngân hàng Nhà nước Việt Nam) is the sole central bank, money-issuing authority and foreign-exchange regulator. The SBV’s Department of Foreign Exchange Management licenses Vietnamese banks to deal in foreign exchange, issues guidance on current and capital account transactions, and supervises reporting from authorized credit institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Vietnamese dong (VND) is a managed, not fully convertible currency for capital-account purposes. Current-account transactions (payments for services, royalties, trade-related charges) are generally unrestricted and may be settled through licensed banks; capital inflows and outflows are subject to foreign-exchange controls and must be routed through a resident entity’s direct investment capital account (DICA). Profit remittance after corporate income tax, annual foreign-exchange reporting, and audited financials is permissible, but requires a bank-approved remittance dossier, tax clearance certificate, and evidence of capital contribution completion.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds from services and goods must be repatriated to a foreign-currency account at a licensed Vietnamese credit institution within 180 days from the payment due date (or the date the receivable falls due under the export/service contract if earlier). Under Circular 15/2015/TT-NHNN, the current mandatory conversion ratio is 0% — exporters may hold 100% of export proceeds in VND or foreign currency; however, the SBV retains the legal power to impose a temporary mandatory conversion ratio (up to 100%) through official instructions in periods of balance-of-payment stress. The LLC must still file currency purchase/remittance reports with the SBV-derived bank reporting system.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Foreign Trade of Vietnam (Vietcombank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) plus Operational Transaction Account (VND and USD)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank for Investment and Development of Vietnam Joint Stock Company (BIDV)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) plus Operational Transaction Account (VND and USD)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Vietnam Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Industry and Trade (VietinBank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) plus Operational Transaction Account (VND and USD)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Military Commercial Joint Stock Bank (MB Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) plus Operational Transaction Account (VND and USD)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Vietnam Technological and Commercial Joint Stock Bank (Techcombank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) plus Operational Transaction Account (VND and USD)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for settlement-only use; Low feasibility as a primary banking or capital-tracking rail. Offshore EMIs such as Wise Business (Wise B2B) and Payoneer are not licensed credit institutions, deposit-takers, or foreign-exchange dealers in Vietnam. They may be used to collect foreign-currency service fees from overseas app-store operators and SEO/ASO clients (e.g., US/EU/SG receiving accounts), then onward-sweep the proceeds by SWIFT/ACH to the LLC’s licensed Vietnamese bank account. Legal constraints: (i) no VND-denominated receiving account may be provided without a local license; (ii) an EMI rail cannot be used for capital injections or profit repatriation, which are reserved for licensed bank DICA/processing; (iii) the flow-through must be supported by the same contract and invoice trail used for underlying revenue; (iv) if an EMI receives payments that originate from Vietnamese resident clients, it would require an intermediary payment-services license under Vietnamese e-payment rules, which is not granted to offshore EMI providers. Accordingly, custody and settlement records should remain at a Vietnamese licensed bank while EMI routes are used only as value-concentration tools.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one legal representative with signing authority (or a validly appointed authorized officer) must ordinarily attend a physical KYC interview at the selected Vietnamese bank branch with original documents: ERCC certificate, tax identification number registration, notarized passport/identity card, board/interim shareholder resolution approving account opening and signing authorities, and original or notarized company seal. Remote opening is not a statutory right and is only possible under each bank’s internal digital onboarding policy; for a foreign 100%-owned LLC, most domestic banks will require a physical in-person visit by the General Director or a notarized power of attorney granted to a Vietnamese-resident authorized representative who attends the branch. If the legal representative is non-resident, the bank may accept an apostilled/consular-legalized power of attorney, but will usually schedule a video interview with the UBO to reconcile beneficial-ownership data. A low-risk digital marketing LLC normally completes onboarding within 7–15 business days, assuming no UBO red-flag triggers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: 100% foreign ownership with no apparent physical operational substance in Vietnam
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vietnam Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC), Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) if any, corporate charter, register of members/beneficial ownership chart, annual financial statements, lease agreement for the Ho Chi Minh City office with utility invoices, photos/video tour, payroll and social insurance filings, and a service sub-contract bundle evidencing actual employees/contractors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border collection pattern of high-frequency small-value remittances from overseas advertising/tech platforms (e.g., through Wise/Payoneer)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master service agreements with app developers and advertisers, monthly itemized invoices for ASO/SEO/localization services, platform payout reports, Wise B2B/Payoneer statements, conversion tables of revenue recognition, and a documented business narrative showing each remittance maps to a named client invoice and deliverable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payments or payments from unrelated beneficial owners into the company account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Four-eyes control documentation, contractual client-identity validation, beneficial-owner identification forms collected at onboarding, letters of authorization from each platform/payor, specific remittance-reference matching, and an internal payment-routing policy that prohibits unidentified third-party transfers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of offshore fintech rails creates unclear source of funds and fiat-currency conversion for AML review
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds questionnaire (completed by each UBO), bank reference letters from parent/affiliate banks, prior corporate income tax filings, monthly receipts ledger traced by client ID, and a signed annual compliance undertaking confirming no illegal crypto, gambling, or sanctions-person involvement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO or director resides in a high-risk jurisdiction or appears in sanction/PE/PEP databases
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid identity documents and residence permits, certified UBO registers, negative PEP/sanction screening reports from independent KYC provider, notarized passports, notarized certifications by a Vietnamese law firm, and a shareholder resolution supplying funds from lawful business revenues.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign parent investors must remit equity contributions from a bank account in the investor’s direct name to the LLC’s Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) at a licensed Vietnamese bank via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for correspondent settlement). The payment must be tagged with the purpose code for 'Foreign Direct Investment Capital Contribution' and must cite the ERC/IRC number and the LLC’s registered capital line item. Before the bank executes, the LLC must present: (i) a notarized board/shareholder resolution on capital contribution; (ii) investor bank account statement showing the remitting account; (iii) the capital schedule in the ERC/IRC; (iv) tax registration certificate; (v) if the contribution exceeds registered capital, a new investment-registration amendment. The DICA then becomes the source of record for local currency conversion into VND at the interbank exchange rate. The bank will require that the purpose code and beneficiary legal name exactly match the LLC’s records; the use of Payoneer/Wise routes for capital contribution is not compliant and will be rejected. After capital is received, the LLC must notify the Department of Planning and Investment within 30 days and update the General Department of Taxation’s registration database.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational outflows for contractor fees, advertising purchases, SEO tool subscriptions, cloud/hosting, and app-store networking settlements should be cleared through the licensed Vietnamese bank using SWIFT MT103 messages for direct outgoing wire transfers; SWIFT MT202 (COV) should be used where correspondent banks execute back-to-back covers. For physical-goods procurement, commercial letters of credit (UCP 600) or documentary collections remain permissible, but the LLC’s service-based disbursements will rely almost entirely on bank-to-bank wires. The supporting treasury dossier includes a signed service agreement, a valid foreign-currency invoice, proof of performance (deliverable/status report), and, when required, a Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT) withholding calculation (typically 1%–5% VAT and 5%–10% CIT equivalents depending on service classification; treaty relief may be available under Vietnam’s double-taxation agreements). Payments for services performed by Vietnamese resident subcontractors should be made in VND through the local clearing system (NAPAS/ACH), preserving FX for genuine cross-border commitments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward contracts (delivery-based) executed with an SBV-licensed credit institution on a documented commercial exposure
FX swaps (spot/forward combinations) for managing liquidity mismatches in USD/VND and other major trade currencies
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) where a real underlying foreign-currency liability or receivables portfolio exists
FX options (purchased put/call, and risk-reversal structures) with a licensed bank, provided the notional is supported by the approved annual treasury risk policy

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs): not permissible as a domestic Vietnamese banking product for VND; offshore NDF hedges may be considered only outside the SBV supervisory perimeter and, because of regulatory and settlement ambiguity, are not recommended as the primary hedging rail for this LLC

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Report (Báo cáo doanh nghiệp) - mandatory corporate declaration under the Law on Enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Planning and Investment (Business Registration Office) via the National Business Registration Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the fiscal year-end; March 31 for calendar-year entities that close on December 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of VND 5,000,000-10,000,000 per Article 60 of Decree 50/2021/ND-CP; failure to file for two consecutive years without just cause triggers forced strike-off/dissolution from the National Business Registration Portal

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual License Fee Declaration and Payment (Lệ phí môn bài) - annual franchise-style business levy
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Tax Sub-Department / General Department of Taxation (tax e-filing portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by January 30; newly registered entities within 30 days of grant of enterprise registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.03% per day and administrative fines under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP; sustained non-payment permits enforced tax collection and suspension of tax registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements (Báo cáo tài chính năm) - statutory filing of independently audited accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Department of Taxation / provincial Tax Departments and the Department of Planning and Investment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the fiscal year-end; March 31 for calendar-year filers; audited copy must accompany submission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of VND 10,000,000-20,000,000 for late/non-submission under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP; repeated non-compliance may result in administrative enforcement and coordinated strike-off action

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Finalization Return (Quyết toán thuế TNDN) - annual tax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: provincial Tax Sub-Department / General Department of Taxation (tax e-filing portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the fiscal year-end; March 31 for calendar-year filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.03% per day on unpaid CIT; administrative penalties of 10-20% of under-declared tax and up to VND 35,000,000 for procedural violations under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP; persistent default triggers enforced collection

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for all foreign-invested enterprises (including this Local LLC), state-owned enterprises, parent companies of groups, listed entities, and enterprises with paid-in capital exceeding VND 500 billion; auditing requirement governed by Decree 160/2018/ND-CP and Circular 26/2022/TT-BTC
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Vietnamese Accounting Standards (VAS) under Circular 200/2014/TT-BTC; IFRS permitted for consolidated financial statements of parent companies meeting eligibility criteria

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Maintain a current member/shareholder register reflecting all contributions; report any transfer or change of ownership or capital contributions to the Department of Planning and Investment within 10 days; beneficial-owner identification and records must be updated and retained for at least 5 years pursuant to the Anti-Money Laundering Law (2022); the Annual Enterprise Report functions as the annual ownership confirmation for the DPI
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard CIT rate is 20%. Small and medium enterprises (annual revenue ≤ VND 3 billion and ≤ 200 employees) may apply a 15% rate for the first two years and 17% for the following two years under certain conditions. High-tech, software production, and supporting industry projects may qualify for a 10% preferential rate for 15 years, a 4-year CIT exemption, and a 50% reduction for the next 9 years. Newly established enterprises in eligible sectors and locations may receive 2-year exemption and 50% reduction for the subsequent 4 years. For an ASO/SEO localization agency (ISIC 7310), the ordinary 20% rate applies absent a specific investment incentive certificate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 01/TNDN (Annual CIT Finalization Return, Tờ khai quyết toán thuế TNDN) filed electronically via the General Department of Taxation eTax portal (https://etax.gdt.gov.vn). Quarterly provisional CIT returns are filed on Form 01/TNDN (quarterly) or Form 02/TNDN as applicable. Mandatory supporting documents include the audited financial statements (for enterprises subject to audit) and the transfer pricing disclosure form if applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual final CIT return is due by the 90th day from the end of the fiscal year (for calendar-year entities: 31 March of the following year). Quarterly provisional declarations are due by the 30th day of the first month of the following quarter. Total provisional CIT payments during the year must be at least 80% of the final assessed CIT, otherwise late payment interest at 0.03% per day applies to the shortfall from the finalization deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax code, legal name, registered address, business lines, fiscal year, and authorized legal representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must ensure the LLC's tax code is active; foreign legal representatives may submit via authorized tax agents and must possess valid digital signatures registered for eTax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B – Incentive and preferential regime declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare whether the enterprise is entitled to CIT incentives under its Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) or Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC), including geographic or sector-based preferences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claims of incentive eligibility must be supported by the IRC; otherwise, standard 20% rate applies and incorrect claims may trigger penalties and back interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report total gross revenue from all sales and services, including ASO/SEO/localization service fees and any recharged costs. All revenue under Vietnamese Accounting Standards (VAS) must be recognized on an accrual basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the LLC invoices foreign clients, all such revenue is Vietnam-sourced and taxable in Vietnam. Revenue received via Wise or Payoneer must be fully declared; failure to declare offshore payment rails is a criminal red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List all allowable expenses with valid invoices/vouchers under Circular 96/2015/TT-BTC, including salaries, marketing, software licenses, subcontractor fees, office rent, and depreciation. Non-deductible items (e.g., unjustified management fees) must be excluded.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to foreign related parties are deductible only with written profit confirmation under Circular 66/2010/TT-BTC and full transfer pricing documentation. Cross-border subcontracting fees must be at arm's length and properly supported.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter tax losses carried forward from previous years, limited to 5 consecutive years. Losses must be applied in chronological order; no carry-back is allowed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign investors cannot offset foreign losses against Vietnamese profits; each Vietnamese entity calculates its own tax loss carryforward.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box F – Taxable income and CIT payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute taxable income = gross revenue – deductible expenses + non-deductible expenses + other assessable income. Apply the applicable CIT rate (20% or preferential rate) and deduct provisional tax payments made during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the LLC constitutes a permanent establishment (PE) for foreign principals, the foreign entity may be separately liable; proper PE analysis is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box G – Tax reconciliation and refund/payment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile provisional payments against final CIT payable. Any additional tax must be paid by the finalization deadline; refunds are processed by the tax authority after audit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Refund requests require complete documentation; pending tax arrears will offset any refund.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box H – Related party transaction disclosure
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose all related party transactions (RPT) under Form 01-TP as required by Circular 132/2018/TT-BTC, including the nature, value, and pricing method for each transaction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transactions with foreign parent, affiliate platforms (e.g., app stores), management fee payments, and cross-border service recharges must all be disclosed. Non-disclosure can trigger deemed adjustments and severe penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box I – Transfer pricing documentation checklist
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirm whether the enterprise is required to prepare Local File / Master File / CbCR based on the thresholds in Decree 132/2018/ND-CP.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parents must ensure the Vietnamese LLC maintains contemporaneous TP documentation in Vietnamese and submits it within 30 days of a tax authority request, or 90 days for Master File/CbCR.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties under Law on Tax Administration No. 38/2019/QH14: VND 4M–8M for 1–5 days late; VND 8M–16M for 6–30 days late; VND 16M–24M for 31–90 days late; VND 24M for more than 90 days. Late payment interest accrues at 0.03% per day on the unpaid amount. Failure to file may also result in forced assessment, suspension of tax code, and criminal liability if intentional.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (Vietnam does not impose dividend withholding tax on distributions by a Vietnamese LLC to its foreign corporate shareholders after CIT has been fully paid. However, profit remittance requires finalization of CIT, audited financial statements, and compliance with State Bank of Vietnam regulations under Circular 05/2021/TT-NHNN. For foreign individual shareholders, personal income tax at progressive rates applies to dividends. Payments classified as interest, royalties, or service fees are not dividends and remain subject to the respective WHT rates.)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a double tax agreement (DTA), the non-resident recipient must: (1) obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the foreign tax authority; (2) submit a written request for treaty relief using Form 02/HT to the Vietnamese tax authority before or at the time of payment; (3) substantiate beneficial ownership — shell or conduit entities without economic substance will be denied treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test (PPT) as implemented by Circular 126/2020/TT-BTC; (4) for dividends, no treaty relief is needed in Vietnam because the domestic rate is 0%; foreign shareholders may rely on foreign tax credits in their home jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory foreign contractor tax (FCT) rates: interest paid to non-residents – 5% WHT; royalties and license fees (software IP, trademarks, copyrights) – 10% WHT; other cross-border services – 5% VAT + 5% CIT under the FCT regime (combined tax burden). Treaty rates vary: under the Vietnam–Singapore DTA, interest 5%, royalties 10%; Vietnam–Korea DTA, interest 5%, royalties 10%; Vietnam–China DTA, interest 10%, royalties 10%. For jurisdictions without a DTA, domestic rates apply. Payments for standardized software are generally treated as royalties; customization/consulting may be treated as services.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: VND 50 billion (approx. USD 2.1 million) in annual related-party revenue triggers the mandatory Local File requirement. The Master File requirement applies when the consolidated group revenue exceeds VND 75,000 billion (approx. USD 3.2 billion). Country-by-Country Report is required when the ultimate parent group is required to file CbCR and the Vietnamese entity meets the VND 75,000 billion consolidated revenue threshold. Even below VND 50 billion, TP documentation may be requested if the enterprise has sustained losses for two consecutive years or related-party transactions are material.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vietnam applies the substance-over-form doctrine via Decree 132/2018/ND-CP and Circular 132/2018/TT-BTC. Transactions lacking economic substance and primarily for profit shifting may be disregarded or recharacterized. The Principal Purpose Test (PPT) under the MLI denies treaty benefits to arrangements with a principal purpose of treaty shopping. For an ASO/SEO agency, economic substance requires actual local personnel, office premises, operational evidence (campaign reports, client communications, subcontractor agreements), and arm's-length pricing. Vietnam does not have an ESR law analogous to the UAE, but substance checks are embedded in TP audits and CIT examinations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating revenue (e.g., receiving payments via Wise/Payoneer into undisclosed accounts), falsifying invoices, inflating deductible expenses, or omitting related-party transactions from Form 01-TP.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 200 of the Penal Code 2015 (as amended), tax evasion of VND 100 million or more is punishable by 3 months to 7 years' imprisonment. Administrative fines range from 20% to 300% of evaded tax under Law on Tax Administration No. 38/2019/QH14, plus 0.03% daily late payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and chief accountants who falsify returns face criminal prosecution, imprisonment, joint and several civil liability for tax arrears and fines, travel bans, and asset seizure. The corporate veil may be pierced where the LLC is an instrument of fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length prices on cross-border related-party transactions, paying excessive management or royalty fees offshore, thin capitalization with related-party debt above arm's length, or lacking contemporaneous TP documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Upward CIT adjustments, disallowance of interest deductions exceeding 30% of EBITDA (related-party loans), 20% to 200% administrative fines on understated tax, 0.03% daily interest, and non-deductibility of undeclared payments. Fines for TP documentation failure range from VND 12M–30M.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for tax debts if pricing manipulation constitutes intentional evasion, and may face civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment if the TP manipulation is criminalized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a letterbox entity with no real office, no employees, no operational substance, while routing service income through Vietnam to benefit from tax advantages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authority may recharacterize the entity, reattribute income to the offshore principal, impose full CIT at 20% plus late interest, levy administrative fines under Decree 88/2019/ND-CP, suspended tax code, and AML fines up to VND 300 million under Law No. 02/2022/QH15.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may face money laundering charges under Article 324 Penal Code with imprisonment of 1–10 years, asset forfeiture, travel bans, and personal civil liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Foreign Contractor Tax / Withholding Tax Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to withhold FCT on payments to non-resident software platforms, overseas advertising networks, royalty holders, or subcontractors. Also failing to register profit remittance with the State Bank of Vietnam.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The LLC is liable for unpaid FCT, fines up to the withheld amount, 0.03% daily interest, fines up to VND 24M under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP, and potential CIT gross-up.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Willful non-withholding may be prosecuted as tax evasion; directors may face imprisonment, civil liability, and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using cross-border payment services (Wise, Payoneer) to obscure revenue, splitting transactions to evade reporting thresholds, using mismatched beneficiary accounts, or facilitating unlicensed money transmission.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines of VND 50M–300M per AML violation, State Bank of Vietnam enforcement, freezing of accounts, criminal liability under Article 324 Penal Code with imprisonment of 1–10 years and fines up to VND 100M.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors involved in structuring payments or concealing transactions face personal criminal liability, asset forfeiture, travel bans, disqualification from management roles, and extradition risks.
